title: Sufficiently divisible positive twists are ample on a quasi-compact Proj open
statement: Let $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring, $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj], and $U\subseteq P$ a quasi-compact open subscheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] [def-weil-open-immersion]. For $m\in\mathbf Z$, write $\mathcal O_U(m)=\mathcal O_P(m)|_U$, where $\mathcal O_P(m)=\widetilde{A(m)}$ is the graded-module twist [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. There exists $e\geq1$ such that, for every $k\geq1$, $\mathcal O_U(ek)$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module] and ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and the multiplication map $\mathcal O_U(e)^{\otimes k}\to\mathcal O_U(ek)$ is an isomorphism [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

proof.text: If U is empty, take e=1; all assertions are vacuous. Otherwise, by the basis and finite-refinement clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion], and quasi-compactness, choose finitely many positive-degree homogeneous elements f_i with U\subseteq\bigcup_iD_+(f_i). Let e be a positive common multiple of their degrees; replacing each f_i by the corresponding power preserves its standard open. The finite-cover conclusion of [lem-trf-proj-common-degree-twist-invertible] then gives U\subseteq W_e, the invertibility locus used in Step 3.

source.place: Tag 01MW proof, first paragraph: finite standard-open cover and d=d_1...d_n; Tag 01M4 (basis and finite refinement).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-proj-common-degree-twist-invertible] to this finite homogeneous cover and common degree e. It gives that every O_U(ek) is invertible and that the canonical multiplication map O_U(e)^{\otimes k} \to O_U(ek) is an isomorphism for every k>=1.

source.place: Tag 01MW proof after the finite cover, clauses (1)--(4).

proof.text: Because the chosen e makes U\subseteq W_e, apply [lem-trf-proj-twist-section-basic-open] with d=e. For every positive-degree homogeneous f, replace f by a positive power so that its degree is a multiple of e; the resulting section of O_U(e r) has nonvanishing locus U\cap D_+(f). The standard opens form a basis by [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion], and the affine-locus clause of [lem-trf-proj-twist-section-basic-open] says that among these nonvanishing loci the affine ones form an affine-open basis of U. Using the multiplication isomorphisms from Step 2, the section may be viewed as a section of O_U(e)^{\otimes r}.

source.place: Tag 01MW clauses (5)--(7), using Tag 01MV and the standard-open basis.

proof.text: Fix k\geq1. Step 2 makes O_U(ek) invertible and identifies each positive tensor power O_U(ek)^{\otimes r} with O_U(ekr). Given any basic open from Step 3, replace its defining homogeneous element by its k-th power; its degree is then a multiple of ek, and its nonvanishing locus is unchanged, while the corresponding section is a section of O_U(ekr). Thus the affine nonvanishing loci of positive powers of O_U(ek) form a basis at every point. Together with quasi-compactness of U, this is exactly the definition of an ample invertible module [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. The multiplication isomorphisms required in the statement are those supplied by Step 2.

source.place: Definition 01PS (definition-ample), together with Constructions Tag 01MW clauses (2),(3).

lean.note: Repair of H3 return at 5ca28b2b65bb: the tensor-power morphism is required to send every tuple of local twist sections on every open to its pointwise product in the homogeneous localization, and IsIso is asserted for that morphism. Pure tensors locally generate the sheaf tensor power, so the formula uniquely characterizes the canonical multiplication map; an arbitrary isomorphism does not satisfy this conclusion. Restriction uses the existing open-immersion restrict functor and its restrictAppIso.
